messages:
julia: quick sync — thinking about a 'token slimming' pattern to reduce long-lived API key surface and unify service auth. sketch: keep a small set of long-lived admin keys, mint short-lived intent tokens for most service-to-service and user-facing flows. wanted reactions before i put up an RFC :thinking:

mike: curious — runtime-derived claims vs minted ephemeral tokens? latency and cache tradeoffs in my head.

sarah: runtime derivation is nice for avoiding extra mint calls but needs a super fast token->claims cache (or schema) and deterministic mapping rules. TTLs matter.

cory: per-request minting gives immediate revocation and clearer audit trail but adds complexity (mint service, authz rate limit, retry/backoff). tradeoff: control vs infra surface.

julia: proposal: hybrid approach — edge/router can mint ephemeral tokens for internal calls when needed, but we also allow a deterministic claim expansion path for read-only low-risk routes to avoid mint churn. the minted token includes explicit intent claims so policy engine can remain simple. :thumbsup:

alexa: for billing/telemetry we must preserve lineage. suggest adding an `X-Orig-Actor` header or encode original principal in the minted token's `parent` claim so we can attribute cost without leaking secrets.

mike: agree on lineage. also watch for metric cardinality — prefer a small set of stable labels (org, project, principal-type) not raw token ids.

sarah: RBAC mapping thought — map minted claims into roles via our existing policy engine (no per-token dynamic roles). minted tokens carry temporary grants but policy -> role translation stays static. simpler for audits.

cory: question about API keys used by external customers (public keys embedded in apps) — do we force full migration to ephemeral? that'll break offline clients. maybe a long window where we accept long-lived keys but shadow-issue minted tokens for the same principal and emit deprecation telemetry.

julia: yep — migration plan: 1) shadow mint for requests using legacy keys, 2) log deprecation + rate-limit escalation, 3) provide SDK helpers to auto-mint for clients that can. keep router accepting both during rollout.

alexa: config snippet idea for mapping rules (pseudo):
```
# mapping rules example
match: project:1234:key:ABCD
mint_to: {sub: "svc:ingress", aud: "model-serving", claims: ["read:dataset:proj:1234"], exp: now + 15m, parent: "proj:1234:user:alice"}
```

mike: need to ensure our telemetry & SSO audit logs get the `parent` mapping. otherwise we lose who actually triggered the mint.

sarah: for enforcement, policy engine should only look at `claims` and `aud`. `parent` purely for audit and billing. keep those semantics explicit in RFC.

cory: ops concerns — mint service must be highly available and throttled per-customer. failure mode: fallback to runtime claim derivation if mint unavailable (with a short grace TTL) — documented circuit-breaker.

julia: exactly. fallback chain: minted token -> cached derived claim -> deny. need clear SLOs for mint service and a canary plan.

deploy-bot: started canary rollout of token-slimmer experiment (eng-sre canary) — https://deploys.internal/redwood/rollouts/3311 

alexa: nice. next steps: i can draft a short RFC covering: token shapes, claim vocab, migration plan, metrics to track (shadow mint rate, lineage lost rate, cardinals), and ops SLOs. can we assign owners?

julia: owner: julia (design + RFC). mike + sarah to review policy/telemetry sections. cory to own mint-service reliability plan. alexa to own migration SDK docs. target RFC in two weeks (2026-04-04).

mike: lgtm. i'll add a short note about reduced label cardinality and instrumentation hooks.

sarah: will sketch the policy examples and role mapping table.

cory: i'll draft failure-mode diagrams.

julia: thanks all — i'll open the RFC draft tomorrow and ping reviewers.
